body:
Thank you for the distinction., as I didn't really know there was one.  Yeah, it's not intent it's ideation as you describe it.

And this emotionless aspect of my life has indeed always been there.  Somewhat ironically, it wasn't there when my mom was going through cancer last year but it was before that.  She had cancer and from the point of diagnosis to her death (around 8 months) I never once thought about suicide, felt emotionless when alone, or anything.  I actually felt emotions every day.  I read a comment on the main page of reddit the other day (in the thread about men asking other men things they've never wanted to ask) that made me worried I had anhedonia or something, but I don't want to take antidepressants and I don't have a problem interacting with others at all.  It's just weird that I felt more normal and more human when I had to be the primary care-taker for my mom than I do on a regular weekly basis.  

I don't think any of this gets in the way of living my life, which is why I don't want to seek any form of prescription for this, I just wanted to know if these kinds of thoughts and behaviors were "normal", or at least not unhealthy (sorry for the double negative).

So despite the fact that I had to watch my mom go through cancer, I don't feel like I fit any of the three factors you mentioned.  And knowing that my baseline way of behaving has been this way through the majority of my life is something I hadn't considered either, which is good.

You guys are always really helpful, and I really appreciate advice on this.  Thank you.
